verdict: UnitedHealth Group grew revenue 2% to $111.7B and held operating profit at $9.0B, as an 83.9% medical care ratio offset higher spending on operations, technology and care delivery.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: $111.7B in revenue, vs $109.6B a year ago

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: vs $6.85 a year ago; adjusted EPS was $7.23

kpis.label: Medical care ratio
kpis.note: Share of premiums paid out as medical care — down from 84.8% a year ago

segments.name: Premiums
segments.note: Health-insurance premiums from members, employers and government programs — the money people pay for coverage. UnitedHealthcare served 49.1 million people in the quarter.

segments.name: Products
segments.note: Prescription drugs and other products sold, mainly through Optum Rx pharmacies.

segments.name: Services
segments.note: Fees for delivering care and for health technology and data services, mainly from Optum Health clinics and Optum Insight.

segments.name: Investment and other income
segments.note: Income from the company's investment portfolio and other small sources.

opex.name: Operating costs
opex.note: The day-to-day cost of running the company — people, technology and offices. At 13.8% of revenue (the operating cost ratio, up from 12.4% a year ago), it reflects deliberate investment in consumer and provider experience, AI and cybersecurity.

opex.name: Depreciation and amortization
opex.note: A non-cash charge spreading the cost of buildings, equipment, software and acquired businesses over their useful lives.

otherDetail: Other expense of $1,027M is $955M of interest expense plus a $72M loss on subsidiaries held for sale (mainly the remaining South American businesses). Investment income is not in this line — it is already counted in revenue.
footerNote: Net earnings of $6,481M include $201M belonging to noncontrolling interests; $6,280M is attributable to common shareholders.
follow100Note: Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Medical costs stayed controlled
takeaways.text: The medical care ratio — the share of premiums paid out as medical care — was 83.9%, down from 84.8% a year ago, on strong cost management and favorable reserve development, even though utilization and unit costs stayed elevated.

takeaways.title: The insurer carried the quarter
takeaways.text: UnitedHealthcare earned $5,694M on $86.3B of revenue (a 6.6% margin), up from $5,226M a year ago, as repricing caught up with cost trends. Optum earned $3,296M — Optum Health $1,141M, Optum Insight $963M, Optum Rx $1,192M — down from $3,893M as it invested.

takeaways.title: Outlook raised
takeaways.text: UnitedHealth raised its full-year 2026 outlook to net earnings above $17.35 a share and adjusted earnings above $18.25. Cash flow from operations was $8.9B in the quarter, 1.4 times net income.

oneTimers: Below operating earnings, UnitedHealth booked a $72M loss on subsidiaries held for sale, tied to the remaining South American businesses it is exiting as it refocuses on U.S. health care.

The quarter's adjusted EPS of $7.23 (versus $6.90 GAAP) excludes items including that loss and restructuring and other charges in Optum; adjusted earnings from operations were $8,964M versus $8,990M GAAP.
